text: Tonight, the Moon is gone. The first thing you'd notice isn't the sky. It's the sea.
The Moon is the main reason we have tides. Its gravity pulls the ocean into a bulge, and Earth spins underneath it.
Without it, only the Sun is left pulling, and the tides shrink to about a third.
Rock pools dry up, and the beach gets very boring.
Nights get much darker, too. And corals that time their spawning by the full moon would lose their calendar.
But the big one is slower. The Moon keeps Earth's tilt steady, wobbling only between about twenty-two and twenty-four and a half degrees.
Without it, the tilt could swing wildly, anywhere from nearly zero to eighty-five degrees.
Luckily, that would take millions of years. Unluckily, when it happens, the seasons go completely bonkers.
So next time you see the Moon, say thanks. It's been holding the planet steady for billions of years.
